title: Lenders are getting pickier about funding AI
dek: Bond buyers, public shareholders and venture investors are each putting a price on the AI build-out this week.

body.head: Bond investors weigh the bill
body.text: CNBC reports that bond investors are weighing heavy AI-related issuance against weaker free cash flow, and that Big Tech could find it increasingly tough to secure funding from debt markets as lenders become pickier. PIMCO, citing Goldman Sachs data, expects the biggest AI companies to tap about $250 billion through bond sales this year.
support: Bond investors are weighing heavy AI-related issuance against weaker free cash flow and uncertainty over how quickly data-center investment will pay off.
Big Tech could find it increasingly tough to secure funding from debt markets critical to the AI build-out, as lenders become pickier over corporate bonds.
PIMCO, citing Goldman Sachs data, expects the biggest AI companies to tap about $250 billion through bond sales this year.

body.head: Public shareholders have a say too
body.text: Anthropic's shares fell 8% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the company's $83 IPO price, according to CNBC, after opening at $111.50 on Nasdaq last Thursday. Meanwhile Canaccord Genuity, Wedbush and Oppenheimer have each initiated coverage with a buy or outperform rating.
support: Shares of Anthropic fell 8% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price.
The AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time.
Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target.
Wedbush analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating and a $120 price target on Monday.
Analysts at Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating on Tuesday, and they set a $150 price target for the stock.

body.head: Banks are customers, not just lenders
body.text: Sierra said on Monday that it raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles its valuation to $30 billion, and it lists BNY, HSBC, Wells Fargo and JPMorganChase among its clients. Bank readers sit on both sides of this story at once, as lenders to the build-out and as buyers of what it produces.
support: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra , co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion.
Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive.

body.head: A question to carry into the week
body.text: If you work in credit, treasury or vendor management, it is worth asking where your own bank's exposure to AI sits: in the bonds it holds, in the vendors it buys from, or in both.
